subject: Response-time SLO exception request & remediation plan
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@finedge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@finedge.com>, procurement@finedge.com
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify hosted API response-time commitments (p50/p95 windows)

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. The procurement team has pushed back on the SLA language in the draft: the contract currently ties p95 to a 1-minute measurement window, and FINEDGE is uncomfortable with that for periodic bursty workloads. They want clearer commitments and a fallback plan if we can’t meet p95 in short windows.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm the exact measurement windows for p50 and p95 we propose in the contract?
- If Redwood requests an exception to tighten p95 windows, what remediation and monitoring guarantees come with it? (we need an auditable runbook and escalation path)

We’re on a tight procurement cadence and would like an answer by EOD Wednesday so we can include it in the contracting packet.

Best,
Sarah Li
Head of Infrastructure
FinEdge Analytics

[attachment: procurement_checklist.xlsx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@finedge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API response-time commitments (p50/p95 windows)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — good and very actionable questions. TL;DR: we propose p50 measured over 1 minute and p95 measured over a rolling 1-hour window for the contract. If you need a tighter per-minute p95, we can support that with an exception but it will require:

- A short-term commitment from FinEdge to a max sustained qps per route (to avoid burst amplification)
- A remediation plan (we’ll outline below)
- Additional observability retention and SRE-runbook guarantees (see attachments)

Proposed remediation and guarantees if FinEdge requests a 1-minute p95 window:
1) Canary & staged rollout: we’ll gate the tightened window behind a canary at 5% of traffic for 48h.
2) Autoscaling thresholds: we’ll bump dedicated autoscaling headroom for your tenant for the first 30 days.
3) Compensating controls: enable prefix/KV caching for your hot routes and recommend a quantization profile to reduce per-token latency.
4) Monitoring & alerting: we will provide an SLO dashboard link, daily p95 rollups, and a daily digest for the first 14 days.
5) Post-mortem & credits: if we miss the tightened p95 for more than 3 non-consecutive days in the first 30 days, Redwood will issue service credits equal to 5% of that month’s hosted usage; detailed post-mortem within 72 hours.

I’ve attached a short SLO proposal (slo-proposal-v2.pdf) and a monitoring playbook (monitoring-playbook.md). Can Monica and Ben add the technical feasibility notes and an expected cost delta for the tightened window?

We can sign off on this by the end of this week if FinEdge agrees to the limited traffic envelope and the ramp plan.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Success (Hosted)
Redwood Inference

[attachment: slo-proposal-v2.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@finedge.com>, Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@finedge.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API response-time commitments (p50/p95 windows)

Marcus/Monica/Sarah —

Quick technical notes from infra:
- 1-minute p95 is achievable on our hosted tier for common request patterns, but cost and resource reservations scale non-linearly with concurrency variance.
- For workloads with high variability (short bursts of many concurrent small requests), we strongly recommend:
  * limiting per-route concurrency via client-side throttles, or
  * enabling our request coalescing and prefix caching feature.
- Expected bill impact for the 30-day headroom increase is ~18–28% on tokens for the affected routes (depends on request size & vectorization).

Monitoring/playbook additions I’ll add:
- A synthetic probe plan (1 probe/min for key routes)
- SRE runbook with automatic fallback to the p95=1-hour window after X detected anomalies
- Pager schedule escalation: primary SRE -> on-call platform lead -> customer success manager (Marcus)

I’ll update monitoring-playbook.md and push it to the Drive link Marcus added.

Ben
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API response-time commitments (p50/p95 windows)

All —

I reviewed Marcus and Ben’s plan. I approve the exception to offer a 1-minute p95 window under the following commercial and operational guardrails:

- Timeboxed exception: 90-day review period, with an SLO regression check at day 30 and day 90.
- Cost pass-through option: if the observed cost delta exceeds 25% over baseline we reserve the right to convert the headroom to a billed line item (procurement aware).
- Auditability: Redwood must provide daily digest exports to FinEdge during the review period and a shared post-mortem template.
- Cancellation: FinEdge may revert to the standard 1-hour p95 at any time with 3 business days’ notice.

Marcus — please prepare the short addendum language for procurement (1 paragraph + appendix referencing monitoring-playbook.md and slo-proposal-v2.pdf). Sarah/Procurement — if that aligns, we’ll get legal to bake it into the purchase order.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
